title: Adaptive Disentangled Transformer for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation seeks to mine time-aware user interests by modeling sequential behaviors.

gap.claim: Existing Transformer architectures lack explicit regularization for layer-wise disentanglement, limiting the use of disentangled representations and resulting in suboptimal recommendation performance.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes the Adaptive Disentangled Transformer framework, which adaptively determines the degree of disentanglement of attention heads across layers.

The framework encourages disentanglement using an independence constraint based on mutual information estimation over attention heads and auxiliary objectives intended to prevent information collapse into useless noise.
The framework uses a progressive scheduler to adaptively adjust disentanglement-control weights through an evolutionary process.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on various real-world datasets demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed ADT framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation models time-aware user interests from sequential behaviors, and Transformer architectures are effective for capturing sequential relations.
Existing Transformer architectures do not explicitly regularize layer-wise disentanglement, which is associated with suboptimal performance.
The paper introduces ADT to adaptively determine the disentanglement degree of attention heads across layers.
ADT promotes disentanglement through mutual-information-based independence constraints, auxiliary objectives, and a progressive scheduler for adaptive weight adjustment.
The authors report effectiveness based on experiments across various real-world datasets.

source_observation.claim: The proposed framework adaptively controls the degree of layer-wise disentanglement rather than imposing a fixed degree across layers.

interpretation.claim: Adaptive control may help match representation constraints to the differing roles of layers in a sequential model.

application.claim: When adding disentanglement constraints to layered sequential models, consider layer-specific adaptive scheduling instead of uniform regularization.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that adaptive disentanglement is beneficial for tasks or architectures beyond the reported sequential recommendation setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for mutual information estimation, auxiliary objectives, or the progressive scheduler.
The abstract does not report computational cost, reproducibility information, or limitations.
